# Notion API: integration analysis

> Generated by API Integration Scout from <https://developers.notion.com/reference/intro> on 2026-10-07T14:18:31.755Z.
> Every finding is marked **Documented** (quoted from the docs and verified), **Inferred** (the agent's reasoning) or **Not found in docs**.

The Notion REST API lets connections (integrations) read and write Notion pages, databases/data sources, blocks, comments, users and files. It uses JSON over HTTPS, bearer-token auth, cursor-based pagination, date-based versioning via a required header, and webhooks for change events.

## At a glance

| Area | Finding | Status | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Base URL | https://api.notion.com | Documented | [/reference/intro](https://developers.notion.com/reference/intro) |
| Authentication | bearer: Bearer token: internal connection API token, OAuth access token from a public connection, or a personal access token. | Documented | [/reference/intro](https://developers.notion.com/reference/intro) |
| Pagination | cursor: Pass next_cursor as start_cursor (query string for GET, body for POST); page_size max 100. Treat cursors as opaque. | Documented | [/reference/intro](https://developers.notion.com/reference/intro) |
| Rate limits | Per connection: 600 req/min (Business/Enterprise), 180 req/min (other plans); plus a shared per-workspace limit and some per-endpoint limits | Documented | [/reference/request-limits](https://developers.notion.com/reference/request-limits) |
| Webhooks | Yes: page.created, page.properties_updated, page.content_updated, page.moved, page.deleted, page.undeleted, page.locked, page.unlocked, database.created, database.content_updated, database.schema_updated, data_source.created, data_source.content_updated, data_source.schema_updated, comment.created, comment.updated, comment.deleted | Documented | [/reference/webhooks-events-delivery](https://developers.notion.com/reference/webhooks-events-delivery) |
| Error format | JSON error object with object=error, HTTP status, a stable string code, a message, and optional additional_data (e.g. retry guidance, rate_limit_reason). | Documented | [/reference/status-codes](https://developers.notion.com/reference/status-codes) |
| Versioning | header (2026-03-11) | Documented | [/reference/versioning](https://developers.notion.com/reference/versioning) |
| Endpoints | 5 found | 2 documented, 3 inferred | — |

## Risks

- **HIGH**: Write may succeed despite 503. A write can save and still return 503. Check additional_data.retry_guidance and read the object before retrying, or you may duplicate it.
- **MEDIUM**: Webhook events are signals only and unordered. Events are aggregated, may arrive out of order, and carry no full content. Re-fetch current state and order by timestamp.
- **MEDIUM**: Rate limits are shared and may change. There is also a per-workspace limit with Retry-After possibly over a minute, and Notion plans to adjust limits.
- **MEDIUM**: Notion-Version header required. Requests without it return 400 missing_version. Newer versions (e.g. 2025-09-03 data sources) change endpoints and webhook event types.
- **LOW**: Resources must be shared with the connection. Unshared resources return 404 object_not_found, which is easily mistaken for a bad ID.
- **LOW**: Payload size limits. Maximum 1000 blocks and 500KB per request, plus property-level limits (e.g. 2000 characters of rich text).
- **LOW**: Several endpoint paths unverified. Only 5 pages were fetched, so most endpoint paths and parameters were not read from the reference pages.

## Open questions

- How are webhook payloads signed and verified, and how are subscriptions created and verified? The Webhooks overview page was not fetched.
- What are the exact paths and parameters for pages, databases/data sources, comments and file uploads?
- What are the OAuth flow details and token lifetimes for public connections, and how do personal access tokens work?
- What are the per-workspace and per-endpoint rate limits?

## Details

### Base URL

`https://api.notion.com`

**Status:** Documented
> "The base URL to send all API requests is https://api.notion.com."
> — [https://developers.notion.com/reference/intro](https://developers.notion.com/reference/intro)

### Authentication (primary)

- Type: bearer
- Location: header
- Parameter: `Authorization`
- Bearer token: internal connection API token, OAuth access token from a public connection, or a personal access token.

**Status:** Documented
> "A bearer token is required to interact with the Notion API."
> — [https://developers.notion.com/reference/intro](https://developers.notion.com/reference/intro)

### Endpoints

| Method | Path | Purpose | Key params | Status | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| POST | `/v1/data_sources/{data_source_id}/query` | Query a data source (paginated) | `data_source_id` (path, required), `start_cursor` (body) | Documented | [/reference/intro](https://developers.notion.com/reference/intro) |
| GET | `/v1/users` | List all users (paginated) | `start_cursor` (query), `page_size` (query) | Inferred | [/reference/intro](https://developers.notion.com/reference/intro) |
| POST | `/v1/search` | Search pages and data sources shared with the connection (paginated) | `start_cursor` (body) | Inferred | [/reference/intro](https://developers.notion.com/reference/intro) |
| GET | `/v1/blocks/{id}` | Retrieve a block | `id` (path, required) | Documented | [/reference/request-limits](https://developers.notion.com/reference/request-limits) |
| GET | `/v1/blocks/{block_id}/children` | List block children (paginated) | `start_cursor` (query) | Inferred | [/reference/intro](https://developers.notion.com/reference/intro) |

### Pagination

- Style: cursor
- Parameters: `start_cursor`, `page_size`, `has_more`, `next_cursor`
- Pass next_cursor as start_cursor (query string for GET, body for POST); page_size max 100. Treat cursors as opaque.

**Status:** Documented
> "Endpoints that return lists of objects support cursor-based pagination requests."
> — [https://developers.notion.com/reference/intro](https://developers.notion.com/reference/intro)

### Rate limits

- Limits: Per connection: 600 req/min (Business/Enterprise), 180 req/min (other plans); plus a shared per-workspace limit and some per-endpoint limits
- Headers: `Retry-After`
- Exceeding returns HTTP 429 rate_limited (529 service_overload when overloaded) with additional_data.rate_limit_reason; respect Retry-After. Limits may change.

**Status:** Documented
> "Connections should handle HTTP 429 and 529 responses and respect the Retry-After response header."
> — [https://developers.notion.com/reference/request-limits](https://developers.notion.com/reference/request-limits)

### Webhooks

- Supported: yes
- Events: `page.created`, `page.properties_updated`, `page.content_updated`, `page.moved`, `page.deleted`, `page.undeleted`, `page.locked`, `page.unlocked`, `database.created`, `database.content_updated`, `database.schema_updated`, `data_source.created`, `data_source.content_updated`, `data_source.schema_updated`, `comment.created`, `comment.updated`, `comment.deleted`
- Signature verification: Not seen in the fetched (truncated) page; see the Webhooks overview page.
- Webhooks are signals only, so fetch the latest data via the API. Some events are aggregated, delivery is not ordered, and up to 8 retries over about 24 hours.

**Status:** Documented
> "we will retry delivery up to 8 times using an exponential backoff schedule"
> — [https://developers.notion.com/reference/webhooks-events-delivery](https://developers.notion.com/reference/webhooks-events-delivery)

### Error format

JSON error object with object=error, HTTP status, a stable string code, a message, and optional additional_data (e.g. retry guidance, rate_limit_reason).

```json
{"object":"error","status":503,"code":"service_unavailable","message":"The change was saved, but the response could not be built in time. Read the object again instead of repeating the write.","additional_data":{...}}
```

**Status:** Documented
> "Error responses contain more detail about the error in the response body, in the "code" and "message" properties."
> — [https://developers.notion.com/reference/status-codes](https://developers.notion.com/reference/status-codes)

### Versioning

- Scheme: header
- Current: 2026-03-11
- Date-named versions set via the required Notion-Version header. Backwards-incompatible changes get a new version, additive changes ship to all versions. Opt-in betas use a Notion-Beta header. URL /v1 is unrelated to versioning.

**Status:** Documented
> "Set the version by including a Notion-Version header. Setting this header is required."
> — [https://developers.notion.com/reference/versioning](https://developers.notion.com/reference/versioning)

## Pages visited

- https://developers.notion.com/reference/intro: 6334 chars
- https://developers.notion.com/reference/request-limits: 11929 chars
- https://developers.notion.com/reference/status-codes: 4531 chars
